mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 1.5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05 in OLS regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% in a month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In a 60-day window where the trigger occurs, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 5% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating economic demand, which elevates corporate earnings expectations and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 20 subsequent 5-day periods with similar INDPRO momentum, SPX 5-day forward returns show no mean outperformance vs. the prior 5-day period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of inflation-adjusted consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) to GDP production (GDPC1) rises above 110 for a month, it suggests supply-side pressures that reduce future discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In regimes where the trigger is met, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in the 1-month change of FEDFUNDS above +0.5 percentage points followed by three consecutive months of FEDFUNDS above 4%, predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days due to tightened financing conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS change > +0.5% in a month and FEDFUNDS > 4% for 3 months thereafter
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS spike (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining labor turnover (PAYEMS) below 1.5% while unemployment remains steady suggests labor market stabilization, which reduces uncertainty and supports positive S&P 500 returns within 20 days.
failure_condition: Over 40 20-day windows with similar PAYEMS patterns, SPX 20-day returns show no mean improvement vs. prior (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly industrial production (INDPRO) falls for four consecutive months below its 12-month moving average, it indicates a supply contraction that raises discount rates and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: In such regimes, 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a continuously falling FEDFUNDS rate over the next 3 months predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20 days as lower discounting increases present value of equities.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreasing trend over next 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns show no statistically significant positive relationship with FEDFUNDS decline (p > 0.05).
